$comment: The GitHub Actions zup's own workflows depend on, tracked by release series.
`version` is the exact ref a workflow uses after `@`: a major series like
`v7`, or a moving channel like `stable`. Workflows read these refs rather
than full commit SHAs, so the file is readable and dependabot can advance
them, and so the ref a project writes is the ref the ecosystem uses.
`sha` is what that ref resolved to on `checkedAt`. It is a record, not a
constraint: its job is to make a *moved tag* visible. A ref that pointed at a
different commit than the one recorded here is the one failure mode a
version ref cannot show you on its own, so it is checked.
Read with `cargo xtask github-action-pins check`, updated with
`zup ci github generate` never touch this file: generating a workflow is
offline and byte-reproducible, and a pin that moved under a developer who
was only regenerating a matrix is a supply-chain change they did not make.
